prerequisites: Basic knowledge of basic arithmetic, differential calculus, and integral calculus.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Identify new challenges, projects or improvement opportunities in the discipline aligned with future trends and advances.
Know the different data analysis techniques.
Know how to apply the corresponding analysis technique in each case.
Know how to summarize the information contained in a data set using a few summary figures.

syllabus_topics: Unidimensional frequency distributions. Numerical and graphical representation. Ungrouped distribution. Grouped distribution
Central measures of position: mean, median, and mode
Absolute: range, mean deviation, variance, standard deviation
Measures of shape: skewness and kurtosis coefficients
Joint distribution. Numerical and graphical representation
Measures of linear dependence. Covariance and correlation coefficient
Correlation. Measure of goodness of fit
Experiments and events. Operations between events. Sample space
Definition of random variable. Type of random variables: discrete and continuous
Probability distribution for discrete random variables: Probability mass function
Probability distribution for discrete random variables: Cumulative distribution function
Probability distribution for continuous random variables: Probability density function
Probability distribution for continuous random variables: Cumulative distribution function
Joint probability distribution of discrete variables
Joint probability distribution of continuous variables
Independence of variables. Linear transformations of random variables
Vector of mean values and variance-covariance matrix
teaching_methods: Lectures: Content exposition by the faculty
Practical classes: Group work sessions supervised by the faculty
Teamwork/Integrated project: Carrying out a project to solve a problem or address a task
Tutoring: Personalized and small group attention
Group work: Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects
assessment_rules: The final grade in the first sitting is composed of a written exam (75%) and an integrated project (25%). A partial exam covering topics up to 4 or 5 is eliminatory (with a grade of 5 or more) and accounts for 37.5% of the final grade. For the integrated project grade to be considered, the average exam grade must be 4.5 or more. For the final exam's average grade, the average grade for each part must be 4 or more. In the second sitting, the grading system will be a 100% written exam, or optionally a written exam (75%) and the integrated project (25%), with the condition that the average exam grade must be 4.5 or more for the project grade to be considered.
